outcome: The work item can check what happened, resume or cancel, and pause or continue background work, live
acceptance_criteria: `/work/4107` (mock) shows a "Check what happened" button and no Resume, Cancel or background button; `/work/4111` shows no controls row, no heading and no empty gap — verify: open both pages; `frontend/e2e/work-item-controls.spec.ts` asserts the buttons by name and the absence of the row.

Pressing "Check what happened" sends exactly one `POST /api/v1/work/4107/actions` with body `{"action":"reconcile","expected_revision":5}`: no `outcome`, no `evidence_id`, no `case_revision`, no key — verify: e2e captures the request body; unit test on `workItemCommands`.

After the 202 the item is re-read and the page shows the returned state: with the mock returning `ready` the tag reads "Ready" and the Callout reads "Checked. This item is now: Ready."; with `awaiting_reconciliation` the tag stays and the Callout says so. No outcome panel, no delivered / not delivered choice and no proof upload appears anywhere — verify: e2e on both mock outcomes; DOM has no radio or file input.

If the re-read after a 202 fails, the page says "Sent. We couldn't reload the item; reload the page to see its state." and all controls stay disabled — verify: unit test of `useWorkCommand` with a failing reload.

`/work/4108` shows Resume and Cancel. Resume sends one `POST /api/v1/work/4108/control` `{"action":"resume","expected_revision":3}`; after the 200 and re-read the tag shows the new state — verify: e2e with request capture.

Pressing Cancel opens the dialog "Cancel this work?" and sends nothing; "Keep it" closes it with no request; "Cancel this work" sends one `POST .../control` `{"action":"cancel","expected_revision":3}` and the re-read shows "Cancelled" — verify: e2e counts requests at each step.

`/work/4109` shows "Pause background work" and "Continue background work". Pause sends `{"expected_revision":7,"enabled":false}` and Continue `{"expected_revision":7,"enabled":true}` to `POST /api/v1/work/4109/background`, and neither body has an `action` key — verify: e2e request capture; unit test on the descriptor `body()` output.
`adopt_profile` and `release_invoice` are never drawn or sent, even when the mock lists them in `available_control` or `actions` — verify: unit test on `workItemCommands` with those values listed.

A double click on any button sends one request; while a command runs every control in the row is disabled; a poll result arriving mid-write does not clear the lock or the notice — verify: unit test with fake timers and a deferred POST; e2e counts requests.

`/work/4110` (null `revision`) draws the buttons disabled with "We don't have this item's current version yet. Reload and try again."; pressing sends no request; no body contains 0 or null for `expected_revision` — verify: e2e and unit test.

A 409 `stale_version` re-reads the item (revision now higher), shows "This changed while you were working. Showing the latest version.", does not repeat the press, and the next press carries the new revision — verify: e2e with the 409 scenario, request capture of both presses.

A 403 `forbidden` shows "You can't do this." with the server message and re-reads, with no retry; a 403 `csrf_failed` does not show "no access", refreshes the session once and says "Press the button again", with no second send — verify: unit tests count POST and session calls; e2e on the forbidden scenario.
A 422 `setup_required` shows the server's `message` as given and the first field message when present; the item is re-read — verify: e2e with the 422 scenario.
A 429 and a 503 each say "Try again shortly." and send nothing further by themselves — verify: unit test counts requests over 30 s of fake time.

After a dropped connection or 500 on Resume, Cancel or a background command the item is re-read, the message "We couldn't confirm that this happened. Check the page before trying again." appears, that button is disabled with the sentence "Check the page before trying again.", and no second request is sent by the page; it unlocks only when a re-read shows a different `revision` or the page is reloaded — verify: unit test with fake timers (no request over 60 s); e2e drops the connection.
After a dropped connection or 500 on "Check what happened" the same message shows, the button stays enabled, and nothing is sent until the person presses again — verify: unit test.
A 404 on a write replaces the page with "This record is unavailable."; a 401 shows the signed-out state with a link to `/sign-in?next=` the current path — verify: unit tests with a mocked client.

No write is made by page load, polling or navigation: the only POSTs to `/work/{id}/actions`, `/control` and `/background` come from a press — verify: `grep -rn "liveApi.POST" frontend/src/features/work-item frontend/src/features/workspace` shows them only in `useWorkCommand` (plus F-85's existing upload and proposal calls); e2e asserts zero POSTs on load.

The v7 item path is unchanged: `useWorkspaceStep` tests still pass and `/work/W-xxxx` pages (including `ReconcilePanel`) behave as before — verify: `npm test` and `frontend/e2e/workspace.spec.ts`, `work-item.spec.ts` pass without edits.
`workItemCommands` and `useWorkCommand` have unit tests for the table in Contract: ids, urls, bodies, null-token hold, and the locking cases in criteria 9, 15 and 16 — verify: `npm test` lists them.

Against live Django (8020, Postgres 55433, account live-lead), on an item whose `GET /api/v1/work/{id}` lists `reconcile`, pressing "Check what happened" returns 202 and the page then shows the state `GET` returns; a person for whom the API lists no controls sees no row — verify: compare the page with `oa.py live GET /api/v1/work/{id} 3` before and after; record the JSON of the 202.

Viewport check at 1440 and 390: the controls row has no overlap, stacks full width on the phone, shows no empty gap when absent, and the Cancel dialog fits at 390 — verify: screenshots against the SCR-02 artboards for the parts that remain.
`npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` pass; `api-live-schema-drift.test.ts` still passes — verify: `delivery/checks.sh`.

risk.rationale: High, because reconcile follows an uncertain send, and a retry before reconcile or a wrong revision token would repeat an effect that AGENTS.md forbids. Cancel is hard to undo. The shared adapter in `frontend/src/features/workspace` is the contract the later lines use (contract-change). product-decision stays because the Check button and the live-only-when-listed behaviour change what the client sees (D-182, LC-Q2, LC-Q5), so the client must see the result. There are no payments or external-messaging writes in this slice.

findings.summary: A line form's uncertain lock is lost when its panel re-read fails. `PanelView` draws only the error Callout when `state.status === 'error'`, so `Actions` and the `useWorkCommand` state inside it are unmounted. That state holds the `id@revision` uncertain lock and the unread lock. Pressing "Try again" remounts `Actions` with an empty lock, so a command that just timed out or got a 5xx can be sent again at the same revision. That breaks the spec rule (unlock only on a different revision or a page reload), which the coordinator note extends to every line form. This is the likely path, not an edge case: `useWorkCommand`'s own uncertain branch calls `reload()`, which bumps `attempt` and re-reads the panel against a server that has just failed. Any poll-driven re-read failure (`version` = `updated_at`) does the same. Expected: the lock survives a panel re-read. Two ways to do it: keep `Actions` mounted on the last good readback when a re-read fails, and show the warning above it; or hold the command lock above `PanelView` (per work item). Add a test: a line command gets a 500, the panel read gets a 500, the person presses "Try again", and the command is still locked. | frontend/src/features/work-item/live/LiveWorkItemView.tsx:148-162 and :170-182

findings.summary: `LineActionsProps` has no `onAccessLost`, and the documented example calls `useWorkCommand({ item: ctx, reload })` without one. On a 401 or 404, a line form therefore draws a notice ("This record is unavailable." or the 401 message) instead of the page's signed-out or unavailable state that criterion 17 gives the controls row. Expected: pass the page's `lose` through `LineActionsProps` (for example `onAccessLost`) and use it in the doc example. | frontend/src/features/workspace/adapter.ts:388-394 and :416-421; LiveWorkItemView.tsx:172-180

The one sender POSTs to `command.url` without any check, and the CSRF middleware adds `X-CSRFToken` to every write whatever its host. Today's urls are built from `item.id`, so they are safe. Line descriptors in lanes B and D may build urls from served fields, and the spec allows served URLs only as same-origin paths. Expected: `send()` refuses any url that fails `isPanelUrl` (the read side already does this, in `readPanel`) before it makes a request. | frontend/src/features/workspace/useWorkCommand.ts:53-61

The "Sent. We couldn't reload the item; reload the page to see its state." notice has `kind: 'success'`, so it shows as a toast and then disappears. Every control stays disabled (`busy`) with no reason beside it, which breaks the Button rule "disabled always carries its reason beside it". Only the page's general refresh warning is left. Expected: make this an error-kind notice. It describes a problem, which D-151 allows to stay a Callout. Or give the busy-disabled buttons the reason. | frontend/src/features/workspace/useWorkCommand.ts:93-96; frontend/src/features/work-item/live/ItemControls.tsx:25,40

The unread lock compares object identity (`unreadAt === item`), which fails both ways. (a) A line passes the memoized `ctx` (keyed on id, revision, case revision and state), so a successful re-read that changes none of those leaves every line control locked until the page is reloaded. (b) `run` keeps the `item` from the render where it was pressed. If a poll lands while the write is running, `unreadAt` is set to the old object, `unreadAt !== item` is true at once, and the lock never takes hold. Expected: count reads that land after the send (or compare a load timestamp) instead of object identity. | frontend/src/features/workspace/useWorkCommand.ts:77-79,94

Some tests are missing. Criterion 9 ("a poll result arriving mid-write does not clear the lock or the notice", unit test with fake timers and a deferred POST) has no test. No page or e2e test shows the uncertain-locked button disabled with "Check the page before trying again." beside it: the `wdrop` mock moves the revision, so the tests named "locks it" actually see Resume unlocked. A `w500` page test would show the lock. Criteria 12 and 13 ask for e2e runs of the forbidden and 422 scenarios, and both are unit-only. | frontend/tests/work-commands.test.tsx; frontend/e2e/work-item-controls.spec.ts:118-128

With `action: null`, `body()` spreads `...inputs` first and nothing overrides `action`, so an input can add an `action` key to a body that has none. The server rejects it (`additionalProperties:false`, 400), but descriptor fields winning should cover this case too. Separately, `useWriteLock.unlock` is exported and never used. | frontend/src/features/workspace/adapter.ts:105-110; frontend/src/features/workspace/useWriteLock.ts:45-54

While the controls are locked after an uncertain result, the pressed button still reads "Working..." with the spinner, though nothing is running. Expected: its normal label (Resume) with the sentence; seen at 1440 and 390 on /work/4121 with scenario wdrop. frontend/src/features/work-item/live/ItemControls.tsx

After a dropped connection where the re-read shows a new revision, the page shows "Ready to continue" and the callout "We couldn't confirm that this happened..." together, and Resume and Cancel stay enabled (the mock still lists them). Acceptable per the spec; consider clearing the callout once the re-read has settled so it does not contradict the tag.
